correctness.rationale: Interior vertices in a clique with the same initial color have identical trajectories: when such vertices have state 2, no self-vertex can contribute a state-1 signal, so the inhibition test depends only on bridge endpoint and set of other cohorts. Thus each interior has at most three coherent initial-color cohorts. With 3 endpoint states each, and 7 nonempty cohort subsets per interior, precisely 3²*7²=441 representative state templates exhaust all sizes a,b>=2. The four-block update uses I_u=(v=1 or 1 in P), I_v=(u=1 or 1 in Q), I_P=(u=1 or 1 in P), I_Q=(v=1 or 1 in Q), and advances 0->1,1->2,2->(2 if inhibited else0). Independent integer exhaustive calculation of all 441 templates gives the exact ten matrices of the theorem, with total template counts [3,24,128,24,6,50,42,18,74,72] and maximum first sync 9. The displayed example (u=v=A=0,B=2) first sync at 9 for all clique sizes. Weighting each support-size (i,j) template by exact surjection counts sigma_i(a-1)sigma_j(b-1) proves N_t for unbounded sizes and total 3^(a+b). Full-support/full-support templates have T=2, giving large-size concentration. The finite quotient is exact for all a,b, not finite-size extrapolation.

Uniform worst-case cutoff nine independent of clique sizes, an extremal initial condition and a complete ten-layer distribution are nontrivial all-size dynamical facts, whereas general graph or tree synchronization criteria give no such two-parameter census. The color-cohort reduction is a reusable structural argument.
